read_by: Agent-drafted, from the binding README, binding.json and the source cell's tier table
input: Pressure ratio: (event 3-second gust / ASCE MRI300 reference design gust, 10 m, Exposure C) squared, valid 0 to 2; Strong Wind uses ASCE 3-second gusts, Tornado uses the EF-band midpoint gust; outside the range is unavailable, not clamped
out_of_scope: External access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value)
Overlap with Hurricane wind (not deduplicated; a downstream Total decision)
missing_mechanisms: Tornado-only mechanisms: windborne debris, pressure change, rotation and duration

how_to_use.share_of: Replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts), applied once

outputs.single_event: conditional: whole-station direct-wind damage ratio for a pressure ratio of 0 to 2 and an explicit resistance scenario
outputs.scenario_dollars: conditional: same conditions, damage ratio times the $27.35M fenced value
outputs.yearly_loss: conditional: Hazard supplies frequency, tornado footprint contact, severity and count law, then one station cap; direct-wind screening contribution only

conditions: Pin the source artifact (tropical_cyclone_wind_solar v2.1 docs r2) and this binding by hash
No hurricane duration conversion; inputs are already 3-second gusts
Resistance scenarios are unweighted sensitivities, not probabilities
Strong Wind and Tornado run as independent yearly streams, then one cap of $27,353,236.37
Not a complete tornado loss; unknown event mass kept with tags

method.summary: Same station assembly and same direct aerodynamic loading on a squared 3-second gust ratio, so the hurricane GSU/substation curve is reused as a T4 cross-hazard proxy for direct wind only (see docs/contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_convective_wind_screening_v1/README.md)

key_sources: Canonical tropical_cyclone_wind_solar model v2.1 docs r2, curve TCWS21_GSU_SUBSTATION_SCREENING_T4_ORDERED_STATES
NIST, design guide for the new tornado load requirements in ASCE 7-22
NIST, explanation of tornado loading (2024), incl. Joplin substation damage
NWS Enhanced Fujita scale wind bands
Substation Hurricane screening binding (station and value qualification)
judgment: Tornado EF-midpoint gust used on the pressure axis
Equivalent-square footprint, uniform value and parallel path overlap for tornado contact
GSU-to-transmission-yard transfer and fenced civil membership carried from the Hurricane binding
open_items: A complete tornado response needs the deferred component and pathway research
Regional Fano factor kept after contact thinning (not an exact derivation)
Strong Wind and Hurricane overlap left to a downstream Total decision

rows.variants: pathway: strong wind or tornado direct loading; resistance: lower, central or upper (unweighted)
rows.shape_basis: Source medians and beta are T4; the cross-hazard transfer is also T4
rows.cost_basis: Source state costs 0 / 0.08 / 0.35 / 1 are T4; fenced value membership is T4

notes.text: Direct wind only; tornado debris and pressure-change damage left out
